title: Melanzane Funghetto
subtitle: Neapolitan aubergine cooked like mushrooms with tomato and capers
excerpt: Aubergine is cut into small cubes and fried until it collapses and turns deeply savoury, in the style of cooked mushrooms. Tomato, capers, and olives make this a standout Neapolitan side or pasta sauce.
sourceNotes: Neapolitan contorno of aubergine braised with tomato and capers in the funghetto style, synthesised from standard southern Italian preparations.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: This improves after a few hours as the flavours meld. Serve warm or at room temperature.

content.text: Funghetto means cooked in the manner of mushrooms, small and well browned. The aubergine needs a hot pan to colour before it stews. Don't salt and drain the aubergine first; the quick fry handles any bitterness.
Heat the olive oil in the frying pan over a high heat until it shimmers. Add the aubergine cubes in a single layer. Don't stir for 2 minutes.
Turn the cubes and brown on the other sides for 3 more minutes. Work in batches if the pan is crowded.
Reduce the heat to medium. Push the aubergine to the sides. Add the garlic to the centre of the pan. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, capers, olives, and oregano. Stir everything together. Season with salt and pepper.
Simmer gently for 15 minutes until the sauce thickens and the aubergine is tender throughout.
Scatter over the basil. Taste and adjust salt. Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.symptom: The aubergine is soft but not coloured.
items.cause: The oil was not hot enough before the aubergine went in.
items.fix: Next time, wait until the oil shimmers and cook in smaller batches.

items.cause: Capers were added without rinsing, or olives were very salty.
items.fix: Rinse the capers well. Taste before adding salt.

items.symptom: The aubergine has absorbed all the oil.
items.cause: Normal for aubergine; it gives the oil back as it cooks.
items.fix: Do not add more oil; wait a minute and the pan will look normal again.
